claim: Failure to pay marking duties may give rise to reverse false claims liability under the False Claims Act, and an importer who knowingly fails to disclose to Customs and Border Protection that its goods are unmarked or improperly marked, in violation of its affirmative disclosure obligation under 19 U.S.C. § 1484(a)(1), is liable under the FCA without having made any express false statement to the government.
initial_reasoning: The citation 41 F.4th 83 is presumed to refer to the case discussed in the grounding context, which supports the claim that failure to pay marking duties may give rise to reverse false claims liability and that an importer's knowing failure to disclose unmarked or improperly marked goods to CBP, in violation of 19 U.S.C. § 1484(a)(1), can lead to FCA liability without an express false statement. The grounding context explicitly states that under the post-FERA FCA, an importer need not make an express statement to give rise to reverse false claims liability, aligning with the claim.
